subject: Crossroads brief: OKR gateways, QBR kit and three unblock requests
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@saasmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Crossroads brief: OKR gateways, QBR kit and three unblock requests

Good morning team — quick, actionable snapshot for this week's exec sync / QBR prep. Keeping this tight so leadership can pick the three escalations today.

Wins (short):
- Redwood Dedicated: two pilot customers signed last week; expected first revenue booking next billing cycle.
- Runtime perf: 6% median latency reduction after kernel update on p4s for short-chat flows.
- Eval harness: baseline prompt set automated; smoke tests run nightly for 8 models.

Risks / blockers (need decisions):
1) QBR artifact parity — Compliance appendix is missing the data-retention table. Request: Laura to approve appended template or I will escalate to Security for a final stamp by Tue.
2) OKR Gateway #2 (Throughput) — Deployment autoscale policy currently mismatches production profile; ops needs green light to relax burst cap (trade: slight cost vs missed SLO). Request: Karthik to sign off or provide rollback threshold.
3) Customer escalation — SaaSMetrics (Tom) reported inference timeouts on long-context reranks; CS flagged as potential renewal risk. Request: Marissa to propose immediate mitigation plan and a 48-hour customer update cadence.

Asks (concrete):
- Laura: approve compliance appendix template by EOD today (attachment: QBR_kit_v1.pdf).
- Karthik: decision on autoscale burst cap (accept / tighten with threshold) by 2pm PT.
- Marissa: a brief mitigation note to Tom + ops runbook excerpt by EOD.

Attachments: QBR_kit_v1.pdf (draft checklists), OKR_checkpoint_spreadsheet.xlsx (current gating table).

Thanks — will fold decisions into the exec slide pack.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@saasmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crossroads brief: OKR gateways, QBR kit and three unblock requests

Dylan — thanks for the crisp note. A few quick replies: 

- Compliance appendix: I reviewed QBR_kit_v1.pdf and the data-retention table looks close. I want the specific retention times for embeddings vs generated content called out (30/90/365 days cadence). I can approve if Security confirms those values; I'll ping Soojin to fast-track. If Security can't meet EOD, I approve a provisional note that we are 'awaiting KMS confirmation' for the appendix.

- Autoscale policy: Noted. Karthik, if you can share the proposed burst-cap number and the rollback trigger, I'll sign off in the 2pm window. If risk of missing SLOs is material, prefer a conservative setup with a short canary.

- SaaSMetrics: Marissa — prioritize the 48-hour update. We need a clear timeline for the customer, and an ask to Engineering for a hotfix estimate. If it's >72 hours to mitigate, we should offer a one-week credit waiver pre-approved by Finance. I can loop in Finance if you don't have bandwidth.

I'll be at the 10:30 exec prep call and will bring the provisional appendix unless Security produces the final.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

On Wed, Mar 1, 2028 at 9:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dylan — thanks for the crisp note. A few quick replies: 
> 
> - Compliance appendix: I reviewed QBR_kit_v1.pdf and the data-retention table looks close.

Update on the SaaSMetrics ticket:
- Root cause: large rerank requests occasionally force tokenization spikes that overflow the per-request KV cache window; endpoint returned 504s under sustained heavy long-context reranks.
- Immediate mitigation (in prod within 6 hrs): tighten per-connection concurrency to limit parallel long-context reranks, enable prefix caching for repeated rerank prefixes, and put a 30s request cap with graceful fallback to a lower-cost reranker.
- Next steps (48 hrs): ops to run a targeted replay of failing requests (Marissa + Ops). Engineering to scope a kernel-level patch if replay shows cache corruption patterns (ETA 3–5 business days).

I'll send Tom an interim note with the above and the commitment to the 48-hour cadence. If the fix extends beyond 72 hours, I'll propose the credit path and loop Finance.

–Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OKR_checkpoint_spreadsheet.xlsx (updated gating comments)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@saasmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crossroads brief: OKR gateways, QBR kit and three unblock requests

Dylan / team — decision on autoscale burst cap: approved to relax burst cap by +20% for an initial 48-hour canary with the following rollback and monitoring gates:
- Rollback trigger: sustained p99 latency increase >25% for 5m window OR error rate >1.5% for 3m window.
- Monitoring: Ops to attach a short dashboard target and an automated alert to the exec channel.
- Cost guardrail: automated spend cap at +10% over baseline for the canary; Finance notified.

Laura — I will post the exact policy JSON to the drive link (https://drive.redwood/policies/autoscale-canary.json) and cc Security for sign-off.

Marissa — thanks for the mitigation plan. Please proceed with the 6-hour mitigations; Engineering, please prioritize the replay job.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
